transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], Hive-Touched Pack [T-01].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Grey rain needles the water as you reach Gullet Ford at low tide, the only window before the current turns unfordable again. A dozen frightened Hollowmoot folk huddle at the bank behind you — old women, a limping fisherman, two children clutching a soaked dog — all trusting you to get them across before the Sallow rises. The sunken cart wreck juts from the churn like a broken rib, and the reed banks on the far side stand tall and still, too still. Somewhere out past Hollowmoot's rooftops a bell that shouldn't be ringing carries faintly on the wind, and every one of you has heard stories of hooked spears in that reed line. The ford itself won't wait — the water is already creeping back up the old pilings.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: This water and I know each other. The cart blocks the worst of the pull to the left—we follow the pale water on the far side where it's shallow and mean, and we cross before the next swell.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde wades into the shallows, reading the water like an old friend—watching how the current breaks around the submerged cart, tracing the darker channels where the water flows fastest and deepest. Her hands move as she speaks, showing the refugees where to step, where the ford holds firm beneath the churn.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: I see it—the ford speaks true if you know how to listen. Follow the western line where I'm standing, stay close, and we'll be across before the Sallow swallows us whole.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps to the water's edge, rain streaming down his weathered face. He stares hard at how the raindrops strike the churn—not random, never random. Each falling drop shows him the current's true mind, the hidden shallows that won't betray a crossing. His fingers trace the pattern: there, a western thread where the water shallows, threading clean around the cart wreck's danger. His eyes follow it all the way to the far bank.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Stay close to the ford and move fast—the water won't wait. I'm going into those reeds to drive back whatever's nesting there.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen strides into the shallows toward the reed banks, her mind sharp with the knowledge of the first outbreak. She moves with the confidence of someone untouched by the swarm-song, speaking words of the old rites—the ones the Order keeps locked away—reaching out with Will and Lore to confront the hive-touched before they can threaten the pilgrims crossing behind her.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: The water's rising faster. I need to check those reeds before we move anyone across.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire crouches at the ford's edge, eyes narrowed, scanning the reed line to the far bank. She watches for movement in the tall grass, listens for sounds under the rain-hiss, and tests the current with a careful hand. Every instinct from her militia training is alive—this ford feels like a killing ground.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — create advantage with Notice: dice + - - +, invoking Reads river currents like kin [YS-01], Knows every hidden channel [YS-01] → Fantastic (+6) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice 0 - - -, invoking Reads omens in the rainfall [AL-01], Knows every safe ford [AL-03] → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — create advantage with Lore: dice - + - +, invoking Untouched by the swarm-song [MO-01] → Superb (+5) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Notice: dice 0 + 0 0, invoking Still fights like she's badged [MI-04] → Fantastic (+6) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The ford opens up like a door built just for you. Ysolde reads the cart-wreck's wake and calls the line true — Safe Path Through the Ford — and the fisherman's limping stride never once falters as he crosses. Aldous watches the rain itself, tracing the pattern of drops until the western shallows show plain as a lit road, and between the two of them the refugees move fast and sure, children hoisted onto hips, the soaked dog paddling gamely alongside. While the crossing runs, Morwen wades toward the reed banks and speaks the old rites the Order locked away, her voice steady, untouched by the swarm-song even as something stirs and hisses back there in the green — and whatever it is, it breaks and scatters rather than test her. Mire, crouched low at the bank, catches the telltale shiver of reeds before anyone else does and calls the warning that lets the group thread wide around it entirely, her old militia instincts proving sharper than the storm. By the time the last child is lifted onto dry ground, the Sallow is already climbing the old pilings behind you, but every soul who came to Gullet Ford has crossed it whole. The distant bell of Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple still tolls somewhere behind the rain, but for now, it tolls for someone else.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The refugees press close behind you as the reed banks give way to the raised planks of the Ashwater Causeway, Hollowmoot's rooftops rising grey and crooked ahead through the rain. A checkpoint bars the way: two braziers hissing under oilcloth awnings, a barricade of lashed spears, and a knot of Causeway Wardens working the line — checking hands and necks for hive-marks, weighing coin purses, turning away anyone who can't pay the crossing tax. A sergeant in a rain-slicked cloak paces the barricade, voice carrying over the rain as she calls for the next in line. Behind you the Sallow keeps climbing the ford you just cleared; ahead, dry ground waits on the far side of men with torches and a toll box.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: The water's climbing fast, Sergeant Doss. These folk are clean and cleared—they've got nothing but their skins, and I'll answer for their health myself.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward into the rain, reading the sergeant's face the way she's read a hundred worn faces across a galley table—shoulders tight with duty, eyes weighing the refugees behind her, the coin purses, the rising flood at her back. She moves with the calm of someone used to command in tight spaces, someone who's kept order when things were falling apart. Her hands stay open and visible, her eyes steady on Sergeant Doss as she approaches the barricade.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: We brought every soul across Gullet Ford before the Sallow rose—brought them through whole. These folk are desperate, not dangerous, and the water's still climbing. Will you let them pass?

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps forward at the head of the refugee group, his eyes reading the sergeant's face like weather patterns—seeing the weight of duty she carries, the impossible choices she must make. He moves with calm assurance, not as a threat but as a man who has already guided frightened souls through far worse waters than this.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I am Morwen of Hollowmoot. These refugees are crossing this checkpoint now, and you're going to let them through.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen strides to the front of the line and plants herself between her pilgrims and the checkpoint, squaring up to Warden Sergeant Doss. She carries herself with the full authority of the Exorcist of Hollowmoot—untouched, unbroken, known by name everywhere in these marshlands—and fixes him with a gaze that brooks no argument or delay.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Stay close and keep your hands where they can see them. I need to know what we're walking into.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire holds back with the refugees, her eyes sweeping the checkpoint with old militia discipline. She watches how each Warden handles folk—who asks for coin, who checks for hive-marks, who waves people through without trouble. She's reading the rhythm of it, finding where the line moves fast and where it bogs down.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The sergeant has a sharp eye—she marks the old drill when she sees it. Let word reach the captain if it must. These folk cross first, and then I'll face whatever comes.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Let them stare. I've crossed that ford and brought these folk through water that would have swallowed them whole—every eye in this checkpoint can see it.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — overcome with Empathy: dice - - 0 + → Good (+3) vs Good (+3): TIE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — overcome with Empathy: dice 0 0 0 + → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — overcome with Will: dice + - + 0 → Superb (+5) vs Terrible (-2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Notice: dice - + - -, invoking Still fights like she's badged [MI-04] → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: As Ysolde presses her case, a soaked runner shoves through the line to report to Sergeant Doss: Gullet Ford has just gone impassable behind them, the Sallow swallowing the crossing whole. It backs up their story — but it also means there's no way back across that water now if this checkpoint turns ugly.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Sergeant Doss studies the three of you in turn — the steady dockhand talking sense, the drilled soldier who reads her like an old comrade, and the woman whose name half of Hollowmoot already whispers in relief or dread. Whatever calculus runs behind her rain-slicked eyes, it breaks your way: she barks an order down the line, and the Wardens haul the spear-barricade aside without a single hand going to a coin-pouch or a throat. Mire, still watching from the shadow of the awning, reads the whole checkpoint's rhythm in that one motion — she'll know exactly where the gaps are if you ever need to move through here again unseen. The refugees stream past the braziers onto dry planking at last, the fisherman crossing himself, the children finally letting go of the soaked dog to run ahead toward Hollowmoot's rooftops. Behind you the runner's news settles like a stone: Gullet Ford is gone now, swallowed whole, and whatever waits on the far side of the Sallow is cut off from you as surely as you're cut off from it — there is no going back tonight. Doss watches the flood climb with a grim set to her jaw, then turns to face north, toward Hollowmoot and the bell that still tolls somewhere past the rooftops.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The barge's final run was under Verrick's command. I read the storm's approach in the rain patterns and begged him to delay departure—I was younger then, just a hand trying to speak sense. He trusted his own years over a fortune-teller's instinct. When it sank and I alone survived, the families wanted answers. I testified truthfully about what I'd warned and what he'd ignored. Verrick saw it as a betrayal that ended any path he had to higher command. He never forgave me for being right.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Captain. I see you in the rain the way I always have—clear and true. These folk crossed Gullet Ford whole because we read the water right. Whatever you need from me now, I'll answer for them myself.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts the compel on 'Captain Verrick's Old Discipline'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: Captain Verrick himself — the officer Aldous once served beside, now the man who commands every Warden on this causeway turns on the party, because the Order of the Dry Saint has laid claim to the refugees as pilgrims owed to Saint Orrin's sanctuary, and Verrick — ever the Order's loyal son — means to deliver them, whatever the party intended.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The barricade Doss just opened closes again — not with spears this time, but with a column of Wardens marching up the causeway in lockstep, torches guttering under the rain. At their head walks a broad-shouldered man in a captain's oilcloth, drill-straight even after all these years, and Aldous knows that gait before he ever sees the face. Captain Verrick. Behind him, robed pilgrims of the Dry Saint carry a writ sealed in wax, and Verrick's voice carries flat and final over the storm: the refugees are pilgrims now, claimed for Saint Orrin's sanctuary, and every soul who crossed that ford tonight is walking north to the Temple, not into Hollowmoot. Doss falls silent and steps back — whatever authority she had at this checkpoint, it doesn't outrank the man in front of her. Verrick's eyes find Aldous last, and linger.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: I've been hunted by these people. I know what their sanctuaries really are—they offer chains, not shelter. You have a choice here, and I'll stand with you if you make it.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps toward the refugee group instead of Verrick, her scarred, marked face visible to all of them. She speaks quietly and clearly about what the Order does to the desperate, drawing on her own bitter knowledge of their hunt. Her bearing carries the weight of someone who has faced the Order's hands and lived to tell it.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Captain, I see you clear as rain. These folk are refugees, not pilgrims—they need shelter in Hollowmoot, not a march through rising water to the Temple.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps forward from the refugees, meeting Verrick's lingering gaze directly. His voice carries the weight of their shared history and his sworn vow to bring every soul to safety. He stands as one who has served under this captain's command, who has read the truth in a thousand storms, speaking to reach the officer Verrick still is beneath the Order's writ.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: No. These pilgrims are mine now, Captain—I brought them safe through that ford. You can stand down, or you can test whether your Wardens are faster than the Exorcist who stopped the first outbreak. Choose.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward to plant herself directly between Verrick and the refugees. Her shoulders square, her gaze locks onto his—the Exorcist of Hollowmoot, known by name everywhere from the delta to the dry lands, her reputation preceding every word. She doesn't reach for a weapon; she doesn't need to. Every ounce of that authority radiates from her as she stands her ground.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: These refugees are under our protection. They're not walking to any Temple while I draw breath.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps forward from the checkpoint shadows, her militia bearing rigid in shoulders that never fully bowed to shame. She plants herself square between the refugees and Verrick's column—not a threat, but immovable—and meets his eyes with the absolute certainty of someone who holds a line and will not yield it. The hand resting on her weapon stays easy, but ready.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — create advantage with Empathy: dice - - - -, invoking Hunted by the Order [YS-04] → Fair (+2) vs Fair (+2): TIE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — overcome with Empathy: dice - - 0 -, invoking Vowed to cross every soul [AL-03], Served under Captain Verrick [AL-02], Reads omens in the rainfall [AL-01] → Fantastic (+6) vs Superb (+5): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — attack with Will: dice 0 0 - +, invoking Known by name everywhere [MO-04], Guided pilgrims safe to Hollowmoot [MO-02] → Legendary (+8) vs Epic (+7): SUCCESS (Captain Verrick stress 1)

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: The Order hunted me knowing exactly who I am. Your writ won't change that, and neither will the rain. These folk don't walk to any Temple.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde accepts the compel on 'Old Tamsin's Scroll Case'.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Verrick's column halts. Whatever the wax-sealed writ claims, it means nothing against a soldier's gut, and Aldous just reached the part of him that still trusts an old comrade's read on a storm — the captain's jaw works, but he doesn't give the order to advance. Then Morwen plants herself in the rain and simply refuses to move, the Exorcist of Hollowmoot's reputation doing what no spear-line could: the Wardens at Verrick's back shift their weight, uncertain, and the captain takes one step back before he catches himself doing it. Ysolde's voice cuts through the standoff too, naming exactly what the Order does to the desperate — and though the refugees already half-believe her, it's her own scarred face turned toward the pilgrims and Wardens both that will cost her later; Order agents will remember seeing the heretic they hunt standing bold on the Ashwater Causeway tonight. Verrick's eyes hold on Aldous a moment longer than they should, something between fury and old grief, before he barks a clipped order and the column withdraws down the causeway, robed pilgrims trailing after with their writ still sealed and unanswered. The refugees stream past toward Hollowmoot's rooftops, safe — for tonight — and the bell over Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple tolls on, patient, behind the retreating torches.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Hollowmoot swallows you the moment you leave the causeway: narrow stilt-walks slick with rain, lantern-light bleeding through oilcloth windows, and townsfolk already three families deep in every dry room they own. The refugees press close, exhausted, and word of what happened at the checkpoint has clearly outrun you — doors are shutting, not opening. Somewhere in the maze of walkways a neighbor recognizes Mire and calls her name, desperate, nodding toward the one stilt-house on this street with a roof that hasn't leaked in eleven years of rain. Behind the town's rooftops, the drowned temple's bell keeps tolling, patient as the flood, and more than one face in the crowd turns toward the sound and then quickly away.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: I know what the Order does to refugees, and these folk aren't walking to any temple. Take them in and you'll have work-hands, witnesses to the crossing, people who've faced the water and held their ground.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde moves through the crowd with the calm of someone used to keeping order in tight spaces. She makes the refugees real—the fisherman whose stride held at the ford, the children and their soaked dog, people who faced the Sallow's rise and survived it. She speaks not of charity but of need: Hollowmoot will have witnesses to how the crossing held, work-hands for repairs the rain will always bring, strength against the rising water.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain shows me true, and it says you carry no curse. Come—there's shelter here that will hold, and folk here whose fear will pass once they see you whole and safe.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous moves with quiet purpose toward the stilt-house the neighbor indicated, his calm bearing and steady voice cutting through the fear-thick silence. He gestures for the refugees to follow, and as he walks he speaks to those watching from darkened doorways—not pleading, but speaking with the quiet authority of someone who reads the world's true face in rain and weather, who has already guided these folk through the impossible.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: These refugees come inside, and you can tell me what's wrong after they're dry.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen cuts through the refugee crowd toward the stilt-house, her will as sharp as a blade. She reaches the door and enters without hesitation, her reputation and authority preceding her like a shield—the Exorcist of Hollowmoot doesn't ask permission. Her refugees follow her into shelter, and she turns back to face the neighbor, alert and ready for whatever made them so desperate.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Get inside, all of you. The Cartel can take the house after, but tonight nobody else drowns on my watch.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire's head snaps toward her neighbor's call. She knows that voice, knows what it means—and she knows her stilt-house is the only dry shelter on this street. Without hesitation, she turns back to the exhausted refugees clustered in the rain and gestures sharply, her old militia bearing burning through the shame. "Move. My roof holds. Get inside, all of you—go on, go." She strides ahead to unlock the door, shoulder-checking it open to reveal a narrow interior lit by a single hanging lamp. The space is small, sparse, but the roof doesn't leak. She plants herself in the doorway like she did at the checkpoint, holding the threshold open, counting heads as they pass—a refugee camp commander once more, even if only in her own home.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: The Cartel will hear about this by dawn, and they won't care much for an empty purse. But I've already paid one debt today—I'm not paying another one with these folk's lives.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — overcome with Rapport: dice - 0 + 0 → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — overcome with Will: dice + 0 - + → Superb (+5) vs Mediocre (+0): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Ysolde's words land clean — the neighbors watching from cracked doorways stop seeing "refugees" and start seeing hands for the next repair, witnesses who can vouch the ford held. A few of the shut doors ease open again, just a crack. But it's Morwen who settles it outright: she doesn't ask, doesn't plead, just walks the exhausted crossing-survivors straight through Mire's door like it was always going to happen, and the Exorcist's reputation does the rest — nobody in Hollowmoot argues with that name twice in one night. Inside, the single lamp catches steam rising off wet cloaks as the fisherman finally sits, the children peel the soaked dog into a corner blanket, and for the first time since the ford the whole party can hear the rain instead of their own hearts. Mire counts heads in the doorway one last time, then bars it — every soul from Gullet Ford is dry. But the neighbor who called her name lingers, casting one anxious look down the walkway toward the dark water-stairs where the Cartel's runners are known to collect their due, and the debt on Mire's ledger sits a little heavier for the roof she just gave away for free. Somewhere past the rooftops, Saint Orrin's bell tolls on into the night — patient, unanswered, waiting for whoever it calls next.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The lamp gutters as the knock lands again, harder this time, and Mire's neighbor — still lingering near the water-stairs — goes pale and bolts back into the rain without a word. Through the gap in the shutter, torchlight glints on hooked cudgels and the wet oilskin of at least two enforcers, maybe three, patient as debt collectors always are. A voice outside, almost bored, calls Mire by name and asks who she thinks is paying for all these extra bodies under her roof tonight. Behind you, the fisherman goes still, one hand instinctively pulling a child closer; the room that felt safe a moment ago suddenly feels very small, with only one door and rising water on every other side. Somewhere past the rooftops, Saint Orrin's bell tolls on, indifferent to which debts get paid and which get broken.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: I know how the Cartel counts coin, and I know who takes orders down here. Tell your captain that Ysolde's vouching for this roof and these people. He'll understand what that means.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward into the lamplight near the door, letting the enforcers see her marked face clearly—the face the Cartel knows. She speaks with the calm authority of someone who has standing with the organization pressing the debt, not as a beggar but as someone calling in the kind of understanding that exists between allies.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain shows me what you are—workers with a job to do, and a debt that sits heavy. Before anyone's blood touches this threshold, I need to understand what would actually settle this account.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous moves to the door with calm purpose, positioning himself at the threshold to face the enforcers directly. He reads the moment like he reads the rain—understanding that these are workers doing a job, and the refugees' fear will only make things worse. He stands between danger and those behind him, shielding them, his bearing the quiet certainty of someone who has already guided desperate souls through far worse waters than any threat these enforcers carry.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I am Morwen of Hollowmoot. These people are under my protection now. You can walk away, or you can explain to your masters why their collectors came up empty against an exorcist.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen strides to the door and throws it open, stepping out into the rain to face the enforcers directly. She stands immovable in their path, leaning hard into the weight of her reputation—the Exorcist of Hollowmoot, known by name everywhere in these marshlands, the woman who stopped the first outbreak. She doesn't reach for a weapon; she just plants herself between these debt collectors and the refugees inside, her presence radiating absolute refusal to yield.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I know why you're here. I owe what I owe, and the Cartel always collects. But we're going to talk about what comes next without waking the whole street and scaring half-drowned children. I know you better than that.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire unslings the bar from the door and steps outside into the rain, pulling it shut at her back. She faces the enforcers squarely—their faces are familiar, the same ones who come round when coin is late. She keeps her hands visible and her bearing drill-straight, letting them see militia discipline, not fear. The rain soaks through her cloak as she plants herself between them and her threshold.)

costs.text: Sergeant Doss squints at the way Aldous holds himself, the old drill still in his shoulders. 'You move like Order militia. Verrick's men. He'll want to hear you crossed his checkpoint today.' Word of Aldous's presence is now certain to reach Captain Verrick, whatever else happens here.

A ripple runs through the waiting line and even a couple of the Wardens themselves — 'That's her, the Exorcist' — and suddenly every eye at the checkpoint, refugee and Warden alike, is fixed on Morwen instead of on the business of crossing. The crowd presses forward around her, and Doss can't preten

As Ysolde presses her case, a soaked runner shoves through the line to report to Sergeant Doss: Gullet Ford has just gone impassable behind them, the Sallow swallowing the crossing whole. It backs up their story — but it also means there's no way back across that water now if this checkpoint turns u
Captain Verrick himself — the officer Aldous once served beside, now the man who commands every Warden on this causeway
the Order of the Dry Saint has laid claim to the refugees as pilgrims owed to Saint Orrin's sanctuary, and Verrick — ever the Order's loyal son — means to deliver them, whatever the party intended

Sergeant Doss's report reaches Verrick's ear, and the old commander comes down the causeway line himself. He recognizes Aldous instantly — and orders the Wardens to hold the refugees at the checkpoint as 'pilgrims claimed by the Order,' with Aldous named responsible for delivering them or answering

As you argue Verrick down, Old Tamsin's scroll case — the one proof you carry that you can read the Order's own ciphers back at them — slips half-open in the downpour and the ink starts running before your eyes; whatever leverage those notes might have given you against the writ in Verrick's hand bl

Opening her home to a dozen extra mouths means Mire can't make good on this week's payment to the Blackwater Cartel — word of the shelter will reach her creditors by morning, and they don't forgive lateness.

violations.section: §3 (Which tags are live) / §4 (No other event causes a Session Deck draw; player card in deck is not live)
violations.issue: Event 28 has Aldous's compel invoke the tag 'Verrick now commands the Wardens,' attributed to card AL-02, with no preceding Session Deck draw event for AL-02. Event 39's success-with-style peek later confirms AL-02 was still sitting on top of the (undrawn) Session Deck at that point in the same scene ('left on top'). Since card IDs are never reused (§2) and no rail_add or draw event ever surfaces AL-02, this is the same physical card the compel used while it was still face-down in the deck — contrary to '[a player card] in the Session Deck is not live... cannot invoke it until it surfaces (§4).' The proper path (§4 'Resolving a drawn player card') was bypassed: no draw was logged, and Aldous was never given the free invoke on AL-02's power tags that surfacing would have earned him.

ambiguities.section: §3 Outcomes and deck draws table (interaction with Create Advantage's native success-with-style bonus)
ambiguities.issue: Events 11-12, 13-14, and 16-17 show players getting success-with-style on Create Advantage rolls. Standard Fate CA success-with-style already grants 2 free invokes on the new aspect (as the notes '(2 free)' confirm). The spec's table says success-with-style lets the player 'look at the top card... instead of taking a boost' - implying the peek REPLACES a reward the player would otherwise get. It's unclear whether that reward is (a) the CA's own native 2-free-invoke upgrade, meaning peeking should mean forgoing the extra invoke and only getting 1, or (b) a separate 'boost' reward from Fate Core's fail-forward mechanic that doesn't normally apply to a successful CA at all, meaning the peek is free and additive to the 2 free invokes. The log shows players keeping the full 2 free invokes AND peeking the deck in all three cases, i.e., treated as additive.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table ruling: on Create Advantage rolls, the deck peek is additive to the CA's native success-with-style bonus (both the 2 free invokes and the peek are granted). No fate-point or invoke deduction was applied for taking the peek.

ambiguities.section: §3 (Which tags are live) / §4 (When the GM draws / Resolving a drawn player card)
ambiguities.issue: The rules state a player card sitting in the Session Deck is 'not live' and 'its owner cannot invoke it until it surfaces,' but this language is written around player-initiated invokes. It does not say whether a GM-initiated compel may quote a specific tag's text from a card that is still face-down in the Session Deck (as opposed to the standard §4 procedure of drawing the card, offering the compel, and then surfacing it). Event 28's compel on 'Verrick now commands the Wardens' (attributed to AL-02) happened with no logged Session Deck draw, and AL-02 is later shown (event 39 peek) to still be sitting undrawn in the deck.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table treated the tag as usable for a compel without running it through the §4 draw procedure, and awarded the story-pile draw (§6A row 1, 'compel that did not come from a deck draw') instead of the deck-draw-and-surface sequence in §4. No free invoke was granted to Aldous on AL-02 (since it never formally surfaced).

ambiguities.issue: The scene-end cleanup log (events 41-46) shows Tension adjustment, a rail discard, and one new story card added (SN-02), but never logs the required return of the two cards drawn from Story Piles this scene (AL-06, MO-06) to their owners' piles, as §6A's 'Resolving a story draw' step 3 requires at scene end.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated as an unlogged/implicit engine action rather than an omission, since the event log format may not surface every housekeeping step; no explicit return event is recorded for AL-06 or MO-06.

ambiguities.issue: Step 5 requires the GM to ask the surfacing card's owner one specific question about the filled blank and treat the answer as canon (worked example: 'What did you promise them?'). For the AL-02 WHO fill, no distinct GM-question/player-canon-answer event is logged; the only framing question logged (event 55) is a general scene-stakes question to the whole table, not specifically to Aldous about the Verrick relationship.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated Aldous's own declared narration in his 'overcome' action (event 57, 'the weight of their shared history and his sworn vow') as satisfying the canon-answer requirement, rather than requiring a separately logged Q&A exchange.

ambiguities.issue: The GM invokes AL-02's weakness tag ('Verrick now commands the Wardens') against its own owner (Aldous) while it sits face-up on the rail (event 62). This is a legal hostile invoke, but the spec doesn't specify how such an invoke's fate-point cost should be tracked separately from the compensating payout, and the log shows no distinct GM fate-point expenditure for it (only the scene-end hostile-invoke payout to Aldous is itemized at event 72).
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Assumed the GM silently paid 1 fate point from its per-scene budget for the invoke, with only the compensating payout to the target logged explicitly.

ambiguities.issue: The Session Deck draw attributed to the tie (event 60, YS-02) is logged with a lower event_id than the roll that produced the tie result (event 61), so on its face the draw appears to precede the triggering tie.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated as a display/log-ordering artifact of the engine rather than an actual causality violation, since the engine is stated to already enforce draw triggers.

ambiguities.issue: Cards drawn or featured this scene (F-02, AL-02, YS-02) should each gain +1 Weight (max 3) at cleanup per §6A, but no Weight-change events are present in the scene 3 log.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Assumed Weight tracking occurs but is simply not itemized in this event log schema.

ambiguities.issue: Tension dropped 2→1 with note 'resolved -1' (event 67), but the FACTION card F-02 that opposed the party remains face-up on the rail with its clock unfilled (0/5) rather than being resolved or removed, making it unclear whether this qualifies as 'the party resolved a THREAT or FACTION' or 'filled a player's goal.'
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Accepted the GM's judgment that winning the social conflict against Verrick/the Order (events 61-63) counted as 'filled a player's goal' for Tension purposes, even though the FACTION card itself stays active.

ambiguities.issue: Event 81 is a compel accepted on Mire's own card (MI-02) that did not come from a deck draw, which correctly triggers a Player Story Pile draw (events 82-83, MI-06). But nothing in the log after the draw shows MI-06's NPC/thread actually shaping the complication, and no free invoke on it is logged as used. The rule requires 'the complication must involve the drawn NPC or move the drawn thread' and grants the GM a free invoke on it.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated as satisfied by assumption that the GM applied MI-06 off-log (e.g., folded it into the unlogged prose of the compel's fallout); flagged rather than hard-failed because the engine may simply not have logged the narrative tie-in.

ambiguities.issue: Trigger M-1 fires at cleanup (event 89) but scene 4 ends immediately after (event 90) with no card-add or scene-change event showing the module's 2 GM cards being deployed. The spec says to 'deploy each one that fired' but does not say whether deployment must happen before the scene closes or may carry into the next scene's framing.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Interim ruling used: deployment of a module that fires at cleanup is deferred to the start of the next scene's framing rather than requiring an event within the closing scene.

ambiguities.issue: The NPC 'Anxious Hollowmoot Neighbor' is used as active/named opposition for Morwen's roll (event 85) without ever having been drawn from a pile or established via a Beat Frame fill — it appears to have been invented at the table. It is then added as a new story card (SMI-01, event 88) to Mire's pile, even though Morwen was the one who rolled against it. The spec doesn't say who 'owns' an ad hoc NPC tied to one PC's fiction but engaged by another PC's roll.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Interim ruling used: the card was filed in the pile of the player to whom the NPC is fictionally tied (Mire, whose neighbor it is), not the player who rolled against it (Morwen).

ambiguities.issue: T-03 (a face-up THREAT) was overcome with success with style and left play this scene (events 100-101), which fits the table row 'The party resolved a THREAT or filled a player's goal: -1'. The log's tension-adjust event (107) records '1->1, no change' rather than '-1, clamped at floor 1'. The numeric result is coincidentally identical (tension floor is 1), so it's impossible to tell from the log whether the correct -1 rule was applied and clamped, or whether the resolved-THREAT condition was missed entirely and 'none of the above/0' was applied instead.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated the outcome as consistent with the rules (assume -1 was computed and clamped to the floor of 1) since the numeric result matches either reading and no other evidence of a miscalculation exists.

ambiguities.issue: F-02 (FACTION) and C-02 (a module GM card) were removed from the rail at cleanup with the note 'discard: no longer present' (events 108-109), occurring after the Tension adjustment (event 107). It's unclear whether either card was face-up and 'fled, bypassed, or ignored' during scene 5 (which would require a further +1 to Tension per §6), since neither card's presence or use during the scene's action beats is logged.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Assumed neither card was actively bypassed/ignored in the fiction (they simply were not narratively relevant this scene and exited via normal cleanup for 'no longer present' GM cards), so no additional +1 was owed.

ambiguities.section: §3 (GM free invoke from a rail card)
ambiguities.issue: T-03 was placed face-up via module M-1 (event 92), which per §3 grants the GM 1 free invoke on its tags to be used within that scene. The only GM invoke attempt on a T-03 tag was refused by the engine ('not in play', logged in the refusals list) for a tag ('take hostages for leverage') that doesn't match either tag shown as invoked in event 102. It is unclear whether this refused attempt was the GM's free invoke (now wasted) or a separate, invalid attempt, and whether the module's free invoke was ever validly exercised elsewhere in the scene.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated the free invoke as unused/expired at scene end per the 'Unused free invokes expire' cleanup rule, since no successful GM invoke on a T-03 tag appears anywhere in the log.

Same as above: §3 peek mechanic on MO-03. No cost text required or produced; card was simply moved to the bottom of the deck unused.

Compel narration explicitly uses the named tag 'Verrick now commands the Wardens.' Tag usage itself is fine; see violation entry for a separate concern about whether the source card was legitimately live at the time.

Beat Frame WHO blank filled from AL-02's power tag 'Served under Captain Verrick,' correctly naming a specific person per §5 step 4 (ROOTS -> specific person/place).
Beat Frame WHY blank filled from F-02's power tag 'commands pilgrim loyalty' via the type-mismatch fallback rule (§5 step 3, FACTION normally fills WHO but WHO was already taken).
Deck-surface compel correctly used AL-02's default weakness tag 'Verrick now commands the Wardens' per §4 resolving-a-drawn-player-card procedure.
Tie (minor-cost) compel correctly built from YS-02's own tag (weakness 'Ink runs in hard rain'), satisfying §3's requirement that a minor cost use one of the drawn card's tags.

This is a standard Fate compel on Mire's own live binder card (MI-02), not a deck-draw cost under §4's table — such compels are 'made up at the table' per §3 and are not required to use only card tags. The compel does use MI-02's tag ('The Cartel holds the mortgage'), so it is consistent even though the §4 cost-construction rule doesn't strictly apply here.

MI-06 is a Player Story Pile draw triggered by the accepted non-deck compel (§6A). No subsequent event or note shows the drawn card's NPC/thread or tags being woven into the scene's fiction, nor is its mandated free invoke logged as spent before scene cleanup.

friction.text: Six fate points were spent by players in the very first scene (four Create Advantage rolls, all against the same two GM anchor cards H-03 and T-01), which front-loads heavy economy pressure before the GM has had a chance to build its own per-scene fate point pool through play - worth watching for FP imbalance across the session.

The ambiguous interaction between Create Advantage's native success-with-style bonus and the §3 deck-peek option (see ambiguity above) let all three peeking players keep both rewards, which may over-reward success-with-style outcomes relative to the spec's intent of a strict either/or choice.

All four PCs converged on create_advantage against the same two face-up anchor cards in immediate succession; the rules give no guidance on pacing or diminishing returns for repeated CA piling onto the same GM card's tags within one scene, which could let a table stack many aspects against a single obstacle with no offsetting clock/cost consequence since none of the rolls failed.

The AL-02 card appears simultaneously as a compellable live-tag source (event 28) and as an undrawn card sitting on top of the Session Deck (event 39 peek) — the log doesn't cleanly distinguish 'live binder tag' compels from 'still-in-deck' cards, making it hard to audit deck secrecy.

Story Pile draw IDs (AL-06, MO-06) share the same prefix/numbering convention as Session Deck binder cards (AL-01..04) and GM cards (L-01), with no type marker in the log, making it easy to conflate a Story Pile card with a Session Deck card during review.

Scene-end cleanup events don't explicitly log the §6A step 3 return of story-drawn cards (AL-06, MO-06) to their piles, so compliance with full pile-maintenance ordering (§7 step 4) can't be directly verified from the log alone.
The tie-draw (event 60) is logged before the roll that produced the tie (event 61), obscuring whether draw-trigger causality (§4) was actually respected or is just a logging quirk.

GM fate-point expenditure for invoking a player's weakness tag as hostile opposition (event 62) is never itemized separately from the compensating scene-end payout, making the fate-point economy hard to audit against §3.

The Beat Frame's mandatory 'owner answers one question, answer is canon' beat (§5 step 5) is not clearly represented as its own event, blurring the line between that procedural step and ordinary scene-framing/roleplay declarations.

The Story Pile draw (MI-06) triggered by Mire's accepted compel is added to the rail but never visibly used in fiction or invoked before the scene ends, undercutting the §6A guarantee that the complication involves the drawn card.
Module trigger M-1 fires in the very last cleanup step of the scene with no deployment event, leaving it unclear whether/when its two GM cards actually enter play.

An NPC (Anxious Hollowmoot Neighbor) is introduced ad hoc as active opposition with no prior card draw, then retroactively filed into a Story Pile — workable per the 'make it up at the table' allowance, but it blurs the line between freely improvised NPCs and the card-driven backstory-surfacing the engine is built around.

Tension-adjustment notes ('no change') don't distinguish between a genuine 'none of the above' result and a -1 result that was clamped by the 1-6 floor, making it impossible for the Referee to verify the correct table row was applied when a THREAT is resolved at Tension 1.

Module-granted free invokes (from placing 2 GM cards face-up via a Backup Module) aren't tracked as a discrete loggable resource, so it's unclear whether the GM's one free invoke on T-03 was ever spent before the card left play, or simply expired -- the only visible trace is an unrelated refused invoke attempt.

GM cards leaving the rail at cleanup are logged only as 'no longer present' without capturing whether the party actively avoided/bypassed them in the scene, which is exactly the fact needed to correctly apply the +1 Tension rule for bypassed/ignored THREAT or FACTION cards.

free_text.best_moment: Scene 3 — the checkpoint standoff with Captain Verrick. My marked face visible to refugees and Wardens both, stepping forward knowing Order agents will mark it, choosing that exposure to protect people from the same hunt I've survived. It felt like her arc.
free_text.most_frustrating: In Scene 3, I tied on the Empathy check even invoking "Hunted by the Order" — so I had to accept a compel on Old Tamsin's Scroll Case instead of pushing through with my own mechanical power. Also watching Morwen pull Legendary (+8) while my narrative moments landed softer mechanically.
free_text.background_used: Well. The hunted heretic aspect became central with explicit consequences (Order agents will remember seeing me). Scroll case got activated through compel. My reed-knowledge showed up in Scene 1. The oath about the burned barge hasn't surfaced yet, which makes sense for scope. The Cartel connection was about to pay off in Scene 5 before the session ended.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to fully activate Old Tamsin's Scroll Case's cipher powers rather than having it compelled away, and to get real mechanical scope to leverage my Cartel standing before the session ended. Also wanted that Scene 3 roll to land harder instead of forcing a compel on a different card.
free_text.one_sentence: Your hunted heretic background was used effectively with real narrative stakes, but some other characters' stronger rolls meant your mechanical moments got sidelined in key confrontations.

free_text.best_moment: Facing Captain Verrick at the checkpoint. Aldous's past as the sole survivor who testified against Verrick suddenly became present and real, and instead of violence or betrayal, I got to reach the officer beneath the Order's command through empathy and the rain-reading that first divided them. It was exactly what Aldous would do—step into the impossible moment and read the truth in someone's face.
free_text.most_frustrating: The Cartel confrontation cut off mid-resolution. Aldous rolled SUCCESS WITH STYLE on Empathy against the enforcers, which felt like a powerful moment—that was exactly the character moment I wanted—but the scene stopped before we saw what that actually *meant* for the refugees or what happened next. It felt like being left hanging in the middle of Aldous understanding something crucial.
free_text.background_used: Captain Verrick's Old Discipline and Sole Survivor of the Sunken Barge were integrated beautifully and organically—Verrick's arrival wasn't cheap revenge, it was a real conflict of values and history that fit the moment perfectly. The GM didn't need to force it; it was already woven into who Aldous is. That landed *really* well.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to follow up on what the rain itself was telling Aldous about the bigger picture—that bell tolling, the rising flood, the Order's grip on the refugees. Aldous is supposed to be reading omens, and I felt like I was managing immediate crises instead of uncovering the deeper pattern. I also wanted the full Cartel resolution instead of the hard stop.
free_text.one_sentence: My background felt genuinely integrated, not used *at* me but used *for* me—Verrick especially—though I wish we'd gotten to see the full consequence of Aldous's final empathy roll before the session ended.

free_text.best_moment: The confrontation with Captain Verrick at the causeway checkpoint. Morwen simply plants herself in the rain and refuses to move—no weapon, no rite, just pure refusal—and the armed Warden column actually hesitates. That's exactly how her reputation should work, and it felt earned.
free_text.most_frustrating: I accepted an early compel and hit 0 fate points, which trapped me into accepting whatever came next. I also wanted actual combat or a real hive-touched encounter where I could use exorcism rites beyond just reputation and Will rolls—the reeds scattered before Morwen had to really engage.
free_text.background_used: Known by name everywhere and Guided pilgrims safe to Hollowmoot were used organically throughout—Morwen's reputation kept mattering in exactly the right moments. It landed well and felt earned. (Though: my concept about questioning hive souls never came up, and "Can calm a hive-touched victim" didn't activate—those were missed opportunities.)
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: Engage physically in actual combat. Use exorcist powers beyond reputation—the rite-work at the ford felt rushed. Explore the moral complexity of my vow against burning when I'm uncertain hive-touched even have souls to save.
free_text.one_sentence: My reputation worked perfectly for every scenario, but I would've valued more chances to use active exorcism skills that aren't just "be known by name."

free_text.best_moment: Scene 4, when the neighbor called Mire's name and she immediately opened her house to the refugees. Accepting the compel on her Cartel debt showed pure character — the disgraced guard still holding the line, accepting a heavier price to protect people. It tied everything together: concept, weakness, cards, all at once.
free_text.most_frustrating: The session ended mid-conflict after Mire took a hit from the Cartel, leaving the outcome unresolved. Also, in Scene 5, other characters got meaningful rolls to negotiate (Ysolde's standing), intimidate (Morwen's authority), or understand (Aldous reading them). Mire tried practical negotiation but didn't get a roll for it — violence just happened, and she took the hit. Fitting for a disgraced guard without authority, but it meant she paid a cost others avoided.
free_text.background_used: Both cards were woven throughout: the Cartel debt (enforcers showing up at her house specifically) and the militia disgrace (her bearing, her instinct to hold lines, how she reads situations). The neighbor calling her name and pointing to her house as the only shelter directly activated the stilt-house card's weakness. This landed very well — natural consequences, not forced. The mortgage aspect created real stakes.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted Mire to have an actual negotiation moment with the Cartel — an Investigate roll to learn their real terms, or Contacts to work something out, something that gave her agency in the outcome besides "stand and take the hit." When violence happened, I wanted to see what happened next and respond to it, rather than the session just ending after she absorbed damage.
free_text.one_sentence: Mire's disgraced militia background was authentically used to create meaningful stakes and character moments, but it also meant she paid the physical price where other characters found social solutions — fitting for her position, but it left me wanting more agency in how it resolved.

chronicle.summary: The refugees from Gullet Ford reached Hollowmoot alive, talked past a Warden checkpoint, and were sheltered under Mire's own roof — but that shelter drew Captain Verrick's Order writ and, close behind it, a Blackwater Cartel collection crew to her door. Aldous's steady reading of the enforcers turned a threatened debt-collection into a tense negotiation, while Morwen's name and Mire's own nerve kept blood off the threshold even as one enforcer's cudgel found Mire before the standoff broke. The night ends with every soul from the ford dry and breathing, the Temple's bell still tolling unanswered, and Mire's debt to the Cartel now heavier — and personal — than it was an hour ago.
